proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the right to dispose of, destroy, or alienate property — one of the three classical Roman-law sticks in the bundle of property rights (alongside usus and fructus). As a Roman-law property right it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a legal person (property owner) by virtue of their externally-conferred legal status as owner. It is therefore a Role (BFO_0000023): its grounding is social-institutional (the legal system's recognition of ownership), not intrinsic to the bearer. It is typed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight, which already captures the Role subtype for institutionally conferred rights.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight (itself a subclass of BFO_0000023 Role), inheriting both its specifically-dependent-continuant character and its institutional/role grounding.
Direct typing under BFO Role to make the BFO lineage explicit, consistent with how LegalRight is typed.

open_questions: Should we also model the correlative obligation (the duty of non-interference by third parties) that is the Hohfeldian 'right' side of Abusus? That would warrant a paired instance of LegalObligation.

Do you want Abusus treated as an individual (the specific Roman-law concept as a named token) rather than a class (a kind of right that multiple owners can bear instances of)? I have modeled it as a class here because common nouns denoting kinds should be classes, but 'Abusus' in historical jurisprudence sometimes functions as a named concept.

Should we model the bundle of property rights (Abusus, Usus, Fructus) as a structured whole, e.g. via BFO part-of relations among role instances, or as a working:PropertyRightBundle generically dependent continuant?
Is the bearer class intended to be any legal person, or specifically a Roman-law property owner? The latter would motivate a bearer restriction axiom.
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus names the right of a property owner to alienate, consume, or destroy the thing owned — classically the third stick alongside usus (use) and fructus (enjoyment of fruits). In BFO terms it is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant (SDC) that inheres in a bearer (a legal person holding the ownership status) and is grounded not in intrinsic physical properties of that person but in the external, institutional fact of legally recognised ownership. This distinguishes it from a Disposition (which would be intrinsically grounded) and from a Quality (which would be a measurable attribute rather than a socially-conferred power). Because existing working:LegalRight already captures exactly this combination — BFO_0000023 Role, BFO_0000020 SDC — Abusus is introduced as a subclass of LegalRight, making it a new class (a kind of legal right) rather than an individual. No new BFO categories are required.
